name: The Ritz-Carlton, Washington D.C.
positioning: Ritz-Carlton hotel in Washington's West End neighborhood, with a Club Level and Equinox Sports Club access
best_for: Travelers who want a West End base near Metro lines and embassies
Guests who like a Club Lounge and spa access

facts.text: The hotel is in Washington, D.C.'s West End neighborhood.
Nearby Metro lines serve the hotel, which the official site calls a Foggy Bottom hotel.
The hotel is close to many embassies and diplomatic offices.
The Saga is the hotel's restaurant, led by Chef Enrique Limardo, serving inventive Spanish cuisine with a Latin twist for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Quadrant Bar & Lounge is the hotel's restaurant lounge, with a focus on mixology and gastronomy.
Rooms and suites have oversized Italian marble bathrooms and views of the West End or a quiet courtyard.
Beds are dressed in Frette bedding and 400 thread count Egyptian cotton linens.
Club Level guests have a private Club Lounge with complimentary food and drink presentations five times each day.
Hotel guests can use the Equinox Sports Club, which has a pool and a spa, for a daily charge per person.

highlights.text: A presidential cookie tasting is held in the main lobby daily at 5:30pm.
The hotel offers a spy-themed tour of Washington, guided by former CIA officers and intelligence and law enforcement professionals.
The Ritz-Carlton Suite has a primary bedroom, a living room with a fireplace, a formal eight-seat dining room with an adjacent pantry, and an outdoor terrace.
The hotel partners with its sister property, The Ritz-Carlton Georgetown, for spa treatments, with complimentary transportation to and from appointments.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide an airport shuttle.
Access to the Equinox Sports Club and its pool is reserved for guests 18 and older with valid ID.
Club access requires an upgraded booking; Marriott Bonvoy Elite Status does not provide complimentary Club access.
